report.source_text: The H&E stained section from the cell-block revealed tumor cells arranged in the form of tubules lined by a dual layer of tumor cells. The luminal cells showed a scant to moderate amount of pale to eosinophilic cytoplasm and the basally placed cells showed a moderate amount of clear to vacuolated cytoplasm. A few scattered mitotic figures and occasional lymphoid aggregates were also noted.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old female presented with one month of moderate continuous low-backache and a longstanding, stable, mobile, non-tender firm right lower cervical lymph node. FNAC of the lymph node showed tumor cells arranged in tubules lined by a dual layer of cells with luminal and basally placed cells, mitoses, and lymphoid aggregates. Immunohistochemistry revealed luminal cells positive for CK7 (epithelial marker) and abluminal cells positive for p63 (myoepithelial marker), consistent with epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma. Despite absence of imaging or clinical course documentation, this morphologic and immunophenotypic evidence supports metastatic epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma involving the cervical lymph node.
